turns.t: Morning. It's these patches. Itchy ones, on my elbows and knees. I've had them a few months.
Tell me more about them. What do they look like?
Red, with a silvery flaky bit on top. They look daft.
Do they flake a lot?
Aye, I find bits in the bed. And they itch like mad, mainly at night.
Have you ever had anything like it before? ~
No. First time. ~
Any changes to your nails, pitting, ridges, anything?
No, nails are fine.
And are your joints okay, any pain or stiffness, especially in the morning?
No, nothing. Joints are fine.
What work do you do?
I'm a scaffolder. I'm outdoors most days, and gloves and knee pads, so the knees are rubbed a lot.
That could be making them sorer. Let me have a look. Roll up your sleeve, and your trouser leg.
There you go. ~
Right. I'm not going to put a label on it today. I'd like to treat them first and see how they respond. ~
Fair enough. What's the treatment? ~
I'd like to start you on a steroid cream, betamethasone, apply it to the patches once a day for two weeks, thinly.
Just to the patches? ~
Just the patches, nowhere else. Wash your hands afterwards. ~
Right. Does it stop the itch? ~
It usually does within a few days. And I'd like to arrange a skin scraping from one patch, to make sure it's not a fungal infection.
A scraping? ~
A tiny bit of the flaky skin, painless. I'll do it now. ~
Go on then.
Done. You'll hear if anything shows. Moisturise every day, with a plain thick cream, even when they're better.
I'm not much for creams. ~
It makes a big difference. Try it for a fortnight. ~
Right. And if it doesn't work? ~
Then come back and we'll think again. ~
Fine. Thanks, doctor. ~
